perspective:
Mason’s available information:

- He is an accountant at a small community center. Martha Moua is a colleague there, a personal care aide; their relationship is professional and not personally close, mainly work-related.
- He reviewed the community center’s financial reports and noticed discrepancies. This made him suspicious and anxious, leading him to suspect Martha might be mismanaging funds.
- He asked Martha to discuss the recent financial report, saying some numbers did not add up. Martha agreed to discuss and asked what discrepancies he meant.
- He told Martha that healthcare expenses looked unusually high and did not match usual spending. Martha said there might have been a misentry and that she would review and correct any errors.
- After reviewing the report with Martha, he concluded the discrepancies were due to a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved and embarrassed about his initial suspicion.
- He thanked Martha for clarifying the numbers and said it seemed to be just a clerical error. Martha said errors happen and she was glad they cleared it up.
- He apologized for his initial suspicion and said he should have asked her first. Martha said it was okay, understood he was being thorough, and suggested double-checking entries next time.
- He then believed Martha was competent, but thought the recurring clerical errors showed the financial management systems were inadequate. He felt frustrated with the system and empathetic toward Martha.
- He told Martha the issue was not her management but the current system. Martha agreed and asked what he suggested.
- He proposed a new, more robust financial system and said he would draft a proposal and wanted her input. Martha agreed to help and said it should address the gaps identified.
- He drafted the new financial system proposal. He was hopeful about its benefits but uncertain whether management would approve or implement it.
- He told Martha he had finished the draft and believed it would benefit operations, but was unsure how management would receive it. Martha said it was a solid proposal, told him to present confidently, and said the benefits were clear.
- He said he would prepare a detailed presentation and asked Martha to help gather data. Martha agreed.
- He presented the proposal to management. He felt satisfied with his efforts but physically and mentally exhausted, and believed he had done everything possible to advocate for the new system.
- He told Martha he thought the presentation went well, he had done everything he could, and now it was up to management. Martha said he did a fantastic job, suggested taking time off, and said he deserved a break.
- He thanked Martha, said he would take a few days off to recharge and reflect, and hoped they would return to good news. Martha told him to enjoy the break and let her know if he needed anything while away.
- He does not yet know management’s decision.
